findings.passage: I don't exactly know the line here. I don't think a citizen should be able to own a nuclear weapon. But, I also think that a well armed population deters tyrannical government. At the very least, anything the police can use against the citizenry should be allowed to be owned and operated by citizens.
findings.note: Answer to a voter-guide question on what restrictions on gun ownership are needed for public safety. Date is the 2026 election cycle; exact answer date not shown on page.
subjects: limits on which guns citizens may own

findings.passage: You know what’s more dangerous than a gun you can see? A gun you can’t see.
findings.note: Quoted by the Spokesman-Review, from his remarks at the council meeting on the city gun ordinance. The story also reports he said he concealed carries and called the law “an affront to people’s rights to defend themselves”.

findings.passage: I think that this fails. I think it’s a miss and I actually think it’s going to make us less safe.
findings.note: Quoted by Spokane Public Radio on his council remarks about the city gun ordinance (C36534).

findings.motion: Ordinance C36534, Gun Violence Prevention for a Safer Spokane
findings.note: Voted no as the Spokane City Council passed 5-2 an ordinance limiting open carry in city facilities, widening where firearm discharge is barred, and providing for destruction of seized weapons.
